headline: A New Yorker Named Service Cleans Up What City Couldn't
meta_description: When Joshua Service saw an illegal dumping site under a Crown Heights bridge, he stopped waiting for the city and cleaned it himself—filling 10 bags in 2 hours.
summary_short: Frustrated by bureaucratic delays, Queens resident Joshua Service picked up a rake and gloves to clean an illegal dumping site the city said it couldn't touch.
body:
When Joshua Service saw mountains of garbage piling up beneath a metro bridge in Crown Heights near Atlantic Avenue, he did what most people don't: he decided to fix it himself. After calling the city's 311 number and watching the Department of Sanitation explain they couldn't clear the rubbish due to concerns about a possible homeless encampment, Service faced a frustrating reality—the city said it would need seven days of visits from the Department of Social Services before cleanup could begin. Comments on his video pushed him toward action: "People were telling me, 'Oh, how about you stop making videos about it, and go clean it yourself?' So I did," he told CBS News. Armed with gloves and a rake, Service worked for about two hours, filling ten trash bags and discovering that while a homeless encampment may have existed there once, others had simply turned the space into a convenient dump.

What makes Service's story resonate isn't just the cleanup itself, but what it reveals about civic frustration meeting personal responsibility. Haile Ali, a Crown Heights resident who witnessed the initiative, called it "phenomenal" and "philanthropic." As Service himself explained, he was simply "a New Yorker, worried about the state of his city." Several passersby even assumed he worked for a city department—a telling reflection of how rare it is to see someone take such action unprompted.

The city's Department of Homeless Services later found a homeless resident in the area and connected them with shelter space. Service's work was noticed by City Councilmember Chi Ossé, who planned to honor him at the very spot he had cleaned. Sometimes, as Service's story shows, waiting for systems to work means nothing changes—but one person with a rake can.
quick_facts: Joshua Service cleaned an illegal dump under a Crown Heights metro bridge
He filled 10 trash bags in approximately 2 hours of work
City said it needed 7 days before cleanup could begin; Service acted immediately
A homeless resident was later connected to shelter services by the city
